subject: APAC demo coordination — SeaBreeze: clarify local date/time and invite
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Amy Lee <amy.lee@seabreezetech.sg>, Satoshi Tanaka <satoshi.tanaka@kairo.co.jp>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 18:00:00 -0700
Subject: APAC demo coordination — SeaBreeze: clarify local date/time and invite

Hi Amy / Satoshi —

Thanks for the interest and quick responses. I want to lock a 45-min demo to walk through latency/cost tradeoffs and dedicated deployment options. Below are two windows we can offer next week from our side (times listed in PDT because we schedule from the US office):

- Option A: Tue May 11, 08:30–09:15 PDT (converts to Wed May 12 00:30 SGT / 01:30 JST)
- Option B: Tue May 11, 17:00–17:45 PDT (converts to Wed May 12 09:00 SGT / 10:00 JST / 10:00 AEST)

I realize showing PDT can be confusing — happy to send invites with the target local timezone explicitly shown. Please confirm which slot works or share two windows that suit SeaBreeze local hours (Tokyo / Singapore / Sydney).

Also attaching a short agenda and a timezone matrix so we don't accidentally shift the date across midnight.

[attachment: SeaBreeze-demo-agenda.pdf]
[attachment: apac-timezone-matrix.png]

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Amy Lee <amy.lee@seabreezetech.sg>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Satoshi Tanaka <satoshi.tanaka@kairo.co.jp>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 10:00:00 +08:00
Subject: Re: APAC demo coordination — SeaBreeze: clarify local date/time and invite

Hi Naomi —

Thanks for the options. Quick note: when I convert the PDT slots to SGT it looks like the options are landing on Wed May 12 local time (so your "Tue May 11" in PDT becomes Wed May 12 for us). That's okay but the team would prefer to keep things on Tue May 11 local if possible (we have a product review on Wed mornings).

Would you be able to propose two slots that are explicitly listed in SGT/JST/AEST rather than PDT? That should help avoid the cross-midnight issue. Also, last time we had a calendar invite where the organizer's timezone made it look like it's the next day in Tokyo — want to avoid that.

Proposed (SeaBreeze local) windows that would work for us:
- Tue May 11, 09:00–09:45 SGT (10:00 JST)
- Tue May 11, 14:00–14:45 SGT (15:00 JST)

Either of the above would keep the meeting on Tue May 11 for our Singapore and Tokyo teams.

Best,
Amy
Head of Partnerships | SeaBreeze Tech
amy.lee@seabreezetech.sg

From: Satoshi Tanaka <satoshi.tanaka@kairo.co.jp>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Amy Lee <amy.lee@seabreezetech.sg>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 12:30:00 +09:00
Subject: Re: APAC demo coordination — SeaBreeze: clarify local date/time and invite

Naomi / Amy / Marcus —

Agree with Amy. The PDT phrasing pushes the meeting to Wed for our Tokyo team which is not ideal because our PMs are in back-to-back reviews that day. Also a small DST note for completeness: Australia recently finished its DST period so Sydney is currently UTC+10 — if you're showing multiple local times please ensure AEST (UTC+10) is used for Sydney to avoid a one-hour misalignment.

If you can propose Tue May 11 slots listed in all three local times (SGT/JST/AEST) we'll confirm quickly.

Thanks,
Satoshi
Senior Engineering Manager | Kairo (SeaBreeze pilot)
satoshi.tanaka@kairo.co.jp

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Amy Lee <amy.lee@seabreezetech.sg>, Satoshi Tanaka <satoshi.tanaka@kairo.co.jp>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 21:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: APAC demo coordination — SeaBreeze: clarify local date/time and invite

Perfect — thanks for the quick replies and the DST reminder, Satoshi. I'll send a new invite that explicitly lists the local times for each site and labels the date as Tue May 11 for APAC participants. Proposed (all listed):

- Tue May 11, 09:00–09:45 SGT / 10:00–10:45 JST / 10:00–10:45 AEST
- Tue May 11, 14:00–14:45 SGT / 15:00–15:45 JST / 15:00–15:45 AEST

Which do you prefer? Once you pick one I'll create the Google Calendar event and include the agenda + a short recording link for any teammates who can't make it. I'll also attach the timezone matrix to the event and mark the invite explicitly in SGT/JST/AEST to avoid client calendar conversions showing a different date.

If you want, Marcus can join the call to discuss our Dedicated capacity and latency SLOs — looping him here.

Thanks,
Naomi
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
